title: Medical Terminology
explanation: Patients describe symptoms in everyday language - 'dry cough,' 'heart racing,' 'throwing up.' Clinical documentation should convert these into standard clinical terms - 'non-productive cough,' 'palpitations,' 'vomiting.' This isn't about sounding formal for its own sake: standard terminology reads unambiguously to any other clinician, and matches how the information will be searched, coded, and billed later. The conversion should preserve the patient's actual meaning exactly - never add precision (like a specific value) that wasn't part of what they said.
examples: 'heart racing' -> 'palpitations' (not a specific heart rate, unless one was actually measured)

knowledgeChecks.question: A patient says their heart is 'racing'. What's the correct clinical documentation, assuming no heart rate was measured?
Why convert lay language to clinical terms at all?
options: So the note reads unambiguously to other clinicians and matches standard coding/search
